name: mem_fs
description: Start MemProcFS on a memory image for the length of one call, do one thing with the file tree it mounts, and stop it: the mount is gone when the call returns, so nothing later can read it; what survives is the files an export wrote and the engine's own stdout and stderr, kept as files (mode 0600) beside the mount. SENSITIVE: memory can hold anything the machine held (command lines, environments, keys, process pages), so mode text and mode export, which write content, and mode list with write_values, which writes the original names, run only as a job run as secret output and only with write_values: true, and write only to $OUT/mem_fs (mode 0600, created exclusively, never over an existing file); this manifest declares secret_output for write_values, so the harness seals the job, and the tool refuses as JSON, before MemProcFS starts, when SECRET_OUTPUT is not 1 or the call is not a job. The manifest of exports is appended to by every call of the job (a second export in the same job adds its rows). secret_values.contains_secret_values is true when the job's output holds values from this call or an earlier one (earlier_calls_in_this_job_wrote_values says which), also in a call that asked for none; the manifest is the record. The byte count and sha256 of an item are of the bytes the system accepted, so a disk that fills leaves a count, a digest and a file that agree, and the status says how many bytes are on disk. Every directory the tool creates under $OUT/mem_fs is mode 0700. The answer is a locator (virtual path, output file, size, status per item) with no content and no digest; sizes and sha256 are in $OUT/mem_fs/export-manifest.jsonl. Names the engine lists and lines it prints come from the capture and are judged before they are shown: a name is shown when it has no invisible character, no component over 128 characters and no 16-character-or-longer run of letters and digits that looks random, and no deny-list or backstop rule reads it as a secret; otherwise it, or the span, is a placeholder with its length (name_withheld), listed after the plain names in an order new every call; with write_values the original names go to $OUT/mem_fs/names.jsonl. Withholding is by shape: a plain password, a pronounceable passphrase or any name under 16 characters is printed. Measured residuals of the name boundary, on planted keys (1,000 per cell; a name alone, then inside proc_<k>.exe, <k>.dll and 1234-<k>), as the share printed whole: base64 and base62 keys 0 to 0.6 per cent alone and up to 2.9 per cent in a process-name context (24 base62 characters 2.9, 20 bytes of base64 1.2, 20 base62 characters 2.4); in an engine line, which a failure shows and which has no allow-list, base64 keys of 16 to 32 bytes 0 to 18 per cent, base62 keys of 20 to 32 characters 10 to 61, a 24-character base36 key 48 to 65 and a base64 key holding / 37 to 40. The prefixes of the AWS, GitHub, Slack, Stripe (sk_live_, rk_live_, pk_live_, whsec_), GitLab and SendGrid keys, JWTs, 40-digit hexadecimal keys and user-info were not printed in 3,400 plants per shape. Not read at all, and printed in every cell tried: UUID-shaped secrets, 16-digit hexadecimal secrets, tokens split by . or : into pieces under 16 characters, word passwords and passphrases (100 per cent); and printed at the rates given: 14-character policy passwords (67 to 100 per cent), base32 seeds (43 to 46), licence keys of five groups of five characters (18 to 20) and 12-character fragments of a bcrypt hash (28 to 31). A name that matters is read in a job run as secret output, with write_values. A failure shows at most the first 20 lines of the engine's output, judged as text; the logs are the files named, each the first 1 MiB of its stream (logs.*_dropped_bytes counts what the engine wrote after that: it is read and discarded, so a verbose engine can neither fill the disk nor stop on a full pipe). mode list shows names, kinds and sizes of a directory, no content. mode export copies the named virtual files byte for byte (never as text, never inside JSON); mode text writes one file only if it is UTF-8 text with no NUL byte and within max_bytes_per_path, and refuses anything else instead of decoding it with replacements. A file over max_bytes_per_path is not exported and is counted; an item that could not be exported says why and complete is false; the counts add up to the paths requested, and a path the worker did not reach is counted not_attempted. Output names write every character outside a small safe set as %XX of its bytes, so two different names never share an output file. One deadline (timeout_seconds, 2 to 480) holds over startup, reads and export; stopping the engine and unmounting after it has its own bounded wait (at most 65 s), so the call stays inside the tool's 600 s. A failure names the phase (startup, read, export, cleanup); the engine is then stopped and unmounted. A signal (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP) ends it with one JSON answer (status interrupted, exit 128 plus the signal) after the engine is stopped and the mount released; the engine also ends with the tool on Linux. A virtual path that resolves outside the mount (a link) is refused for that item, and a link loop or any other failure is that item's status; the other items go on. Whether MemProcFS contacts a symbol server is governed by the job's network policy (a job has no network unless it asks for the run's allowlist); this tool passes MemProcFS no flag about it, and the pinned binary's behaviour in that respect was not verified in this review. It needs MemProcFS, /dev/fuse the process can open and fusermount3 or fusermount, which a sandbox may not provide: the answer says which of these the host has (blocked_by names what is missing). It mounts, exports and measures nothing else: it does not say what a file means, that a region is complete or that a page was resident, and which virtual paths exist depends on the MemProcFS version and the image (list first).

mount.description: Where to mount it: a directory under your own work/<your id>/ (in a job, under $OUT); it must be empty. The engine's two log files are written beside it and kept

mode.description: list (default): names, kinds and sizes. text: one UTF-8 text file written to $OUT/mem_fs. export: the files in paths, byte for byte, to $OUT/mem_fs. text and export need write_values and a job run as secret output

list.description: A path inside the mount: the directory to list (default: the mount's root) or, with mode text, the one file to write out

paths.description: With mode export: the virtual files to copy (at most 1000), relative paths inside the mount

write_values.description: Write memory content to files (default false). Required by text and export; with mode list it writes the original names of the entries whose name was withheld or changed to $OUT/mem_fs/names.jsonl. Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which the harness runs as secret output because the manifest declares it; the answer never carries content

max_bytes_per_path.description: Do not export a file larger than this (default 4294967296); it is counted and named, not cut. Raise it to export a larger file

limit.description: Entries or items shown inline (default 200, at most 5000: a larger value is clamped and the answer says limit_clamped_to); all are counted, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in complete_results

timeout_seconds.description: One deadline for startup, reads and export (default 300, 2 to 480); stopping the engine and unmounting after it has its own bounded wait of at most 65 s
